title: Average Yearly Salary Australia: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your average yearly salary Australia from an hourly rate, including casual loading and super paid on top. Use our guide for 38-hour weeks, tax, and fortnight
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross pay is $52,270.72 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my average yearly salary Australia?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. When calculating your average yearly salary Australia, multiply the casual rate by hours per week and 52 weeks. Super is then paid on top of that casual rate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my annual salary figure?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). So if your annual gross salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund. Your average yearly salary Australia figure usually refers to gross pay before super.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on my average yearly salary Australia?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. You also pay a 2% Medicare levy (with possible reductions for low-income singles). This is an estimate; your actual tax depends on your circumstances.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Average Yearly Salary Australia

When you’re offered an hourly rate or a salary, it helps to know what that means as an annual figure. Your **average yearly salary Australia** is the gross pay you receive before tax and super, calculated by multiplying your hourly rate by the hours you work each week and then by 52 weeks. Most full-time roles assume a 38-hour week, as set by the National Employment Standards.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours a week:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year

This is your gross annual salary. From this, the Australian Taxation Office withholds income tax and the Medicare levy. Your employer also pays superannuation on top of this amount.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above:

Weekly pay = $30 × 38 = $1,140
Fortnightly pay = $1,140 × 2 = $2,280

This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **National Minimum Wage** (NMW) is the legal floor. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. However, most employees are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. Always check the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate because they don’t get paid sick leave or annual leave. For the NMW, that’s $33.05 per hour. When calculating your average yearly salary Australia as a casual, use the loaded rate. Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add 25% casual loading – never type a rate that already includes the loading.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). This is paid on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 to your super fund. Your average yearly salary Australia figure does not include super; it’s an extra benefit.

### Example with Casual Loading and Super

- Base hourly rate: $30
- Casual loading (25%): $7.50 → casual rate $37.50
- Weekly (38 hours): $37.50 × 38 = $1,425
- Annual gross: $1,425 × 52 = $74,100
- Super (12%): $74,100 × 0.12 = $8,892 (paid on top)

## Average Weekly Earnings from the ABS

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 per year. These figures help you benchmark your **average yearly salary Australia** against the broader workforce.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Income tax is withheld from your pay. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (reductions apply for low-income singles using 2025–26 thresholds). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net pay.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Using Our Tools

To convert your own rate, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. For award-specific pay rates, see our [pay guides](/blog). You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) trends and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tips. If you’re a casual, don’t forget to check the casual loading box – we add the 25% for you. And remember, super is always on top.

Understanding your **average yearly salary Australia** helps you compare job offers, negotiate pay, and plan your finances. Whether you’re on the National Minimum Wage or an award rate, the calculation is straightforward once you know your hours and any loadings.
